purpose: Current mock/trend layer for UPSC CSE Prelims 2027 GS Paper-I
rules: Historical PYQs are structural priors; they are not post-2026 mock evidence.
Only mock/test/quiz evidence dated 2026-05-25 or later enters the current mock layer.
Provider marketing claims are stored as provider claims, not predictive validity.
Gated or unseen question text is never inferred.
Official UPSC paper is the source-of-record for the 2026 exam.
Question source attribution is never promoted to UPSC setter provenance unless independently proven; UPSC does not publish setter-source attribution.

latest_2026_style_signals.note: External analytical buckets; not official UPSC labels.

ecosystem_signals: ForumIAS: sectional → comprehensive → simulator → current affairs layers; its public page states 20–25 current-affairs questions per full test.
PMF IAS: large integrated ecosystem with static, current-affairs and 20 full-length simulations.
Testbook: high-fragmentation catalog with 123 GS chapter tests, 24 CA tests, 5 subject tests and 20 full tests.
ClearIAS: NCERT + standard-textbook + CA + full-topic architecture across 40 GS mocks.
Drishti: 15-month current-affairs coverage, static + conceptual application, bilingual delivery, and open mock metadata.
Indian Express: recurring public weekly and subject quizzes provide a current topic pulse; they are not treated as full mock evidence.
engine_implications: Preserve primary subject and current-affairs linkage as separate dimensions.
Maintain a high share of multi-claim judgement formats, but vary surface architecture to avoid template mimicry.
Create difficulty through conceptual depth, ambiguity, statement load, cross-topic integration and elimination burden—not obscure trivia alone.
Use post-2026 public mock ecosystem for coverage gaps and failure-mode analysis, not for deterministic predictions.
Keep a fresh current-affairs layer with recency windows and primary-source verification.
